# The discrepancies by priority

Each record has a priority (`docs/record-format.md`, section 6). When more
than one rule applies, the record has the highest:

| Priority | Rule |
|---|---|
| High | MATLAB Pulseq or pypulseq, at master, can write the condition, and a reader disagrees with the specification on such a file: it crashes, plays or reads another meaning, rejects a valid file, or accepts an invalid one. A writer that writes an invalid file also disagrees. |
| Medium | A reader crashes on a file that the specification allows. |
| Low | Neither: no writer at master writes the condition, and no reader crashes on a valid file. |

A record whose discrepancy master has fixed, but that the last release still
has, is in the last section, with the priority that it has in that release.
Records of status `duplicate` or `withdrawn` are not listed.

| Priority | Records |
|---|---|
| High | 34 |
| Medium | 11 |
| Low | 23 |
| Fixed on master | 1 |

## Medium priority

| Record | Condition | Severity | Written by | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DIS-0001](../discrepancies/DIS-0001-version-section-last.md) | [VERSION] after [BLOCKS], or as the last section | crash | — | The spec gives no section order, so the file is valid. No writer puts [VERSION] late. The C++ reader crashes with [VERSION] last; pypulseq fails with UnboundLocalError. |
| [DIS-0007](../discrepancies/DIS-0007-empty-shape.md) | An event that uses a shape with no sample | crash | — | The spec gives no lower bound on num_samples, so the file is valid. No writer writes an empty shape. The C++ reader crashes; MATLAB fails with a dimension mismatch. |
| [DIS-0008](../discrepancies/DIS-0008-event-shape-length-mismatch.md) | The shapes of one event with different numbers of samples | crash | — | The spec is silent on shapes of different lengths, so the file is valid. No writer writes it. The C++ reader reads past a shorter RF phase; MATLAB fails with nonconformant arguments. |
| [DIS-0011](../discrepancies/DIS-0011-rf-time-beyond-int.md) | An RF time shape whose last time does not fit an int | crash | — | The spec sets no bound on time-shape values, so the file is valid. No legitimate writer use gives a 3000 s pulse. The C++ reader has undefined behaviour converting the time to int. |
| [DIS-0012](../discrepancies/DIS-0012-extended-trapezoid-one-point.md) | An extended trapezoid of one point at a time above 0 | crash | — | The spec is silent on the point count and first time, so the file is valid. Both makers move the first time into the delay. The C++ gradientsAt reads past its vectors. |
| [DIS-0013](../discrepancies/DIS-0013-extended-trapezoid-time-beyond-long.md) | An extended trapezoid time that does not fit a long | crash | — | The spec sets no bound on gradient time-shape values, so the file is valid. No legitimate writer use gives a 1e13 s gradient. The C++ reader has undefined behaviour converting the time to long. |
| [DIS-0015](../discrepancies/DIS-0015-blank-or-comment-line-in-section.md) | A blank or # line inside a section | playback | — | The spec allows # comments anywhere and is silent on blank lines. No writer writes either inside a table. All readers reject a comment in [BLOCKS]; pypulseq fails in np.fromstring. |
| [DIS-0016](../discrepancies/DIS-0016-last-section-no-blank-line.md) | The last section with no blank line after it | playback | — | No writer ends a section at the end of the file. On such a file, which the spec does not forbid, pypulseq fails with AttributeError or TypeError, and the C++ reader loses later sections. |
| [DIS-0040](../discrepancies/DIS-0040-label-noslc-spelling.md) | The label flag NOSLC of the specification, which every implementation spells NOSCL | acceptance | — | No writer writes NOSLC: makeLabel and make_label refuse it. On a spec file with NOSLC, MATLAB read fails with nonconformant arguments and pypulseq with a tuple.index ValueError. |
| [DIS-0041](../discrepancies/DIS-0041-version-value-syntax.md) | A [VERSION] value such as 5.0, an unknown key, or a revision of two digits | acceptance | — | Both writers write integer version numbers. On a file with minor 5.0, which the spec does not forbid, pypulseq read fails with an int() ValueError; it also reads revision 10 as 1. |
| [DIS-0042](../discrepancies/DIS-0042-version-without-revision.md) | A [VERSION] section with no revision line | acceptance | — | Both writers write the revision line. On a file without it, which the spec does not forbid, MATLAB read fails with nonconformant arguments; the C++ reader and pypulseq read it as 1.5.0. |

## Low priority

| Record | Condition | Severity | Written by | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DIS-0002](../discrepancies/DIS-0002-shape-without-blank-line.md) | A shape with no blank line after its last sample | crash | — | The spec ends a shape with a blank line, so the file is not valid. Both writers write the blank line. Only the C++ reader crashes, on this invalid file. |
| [DIS-0003](../discrepancies/DIS-0003-missing-shape-reference.md) | A reference to a shape that does not exist, or a [GRADIENTS] row of shape ID 0 | crash | — | A missing shape or a [GRADIENTS] shape ID 0 is not valid (IDs are positive and name shapes). No writer writes it. The C++ reader crashes only on these invalid files. |
| [DIS-0004](../discrepancies/DIS-0004-rf-time-id-minus-1.md) | An RF event with time ID -1 | crash | — | The spec defines RF time ID 0 only and requires positive IDs, so -1 is not valid. No writer writes it. The C++ crash and MATLAB's acceptance are on an invalid file. |
| [DIS-0006](../discrepancies/DIS-0006-shape-sample-count-mismatch.md) | A shape that decompresses to more or fewer samples than it declares | crash | — | The spec says the decompressed length must equal num_samples, so the file is not valid. The writers compress correctly. The C++ overflow and pypulseq IndexError are on invalid files. |
| [DIS-0017](../discrepancies/DIS-0017-section-twice.md) | A section that appears twice | playback | — | No writer writes a section twice. The readers read a repeated section differently, and the C++ reader rejects one file with a message, but no reader crashes. |
| [DIS-0022](../discrepancies/DIS-0022-amplitude-shape-out-of-range.md) | An amplitude shape with a sample outside [-1, 1] | playback | — | No writer writes an amplitude shape sample outside [-1, 1], because both normalise by the largest value. The readers accept the invalid file silently and play it differently, but none crashes. |
| [DIS-0023](../discrepancies/DIS-0023-rf-magnitude-negative.md) | An RF magnitude shape with a sample below 0 | playback | — | No writer writes a negative RF magnitude, because both write abs(signal). The C++ reader sets such a sample to 0 with no message, but it does not crash. |
| [DIS-0024](../discrepancies/DIS-0024-rf-phase-out-of-range.md) | An RF phase shape with a sample outside [0, 1) | playback | — | Both writers write the RF phase in [0, 1). The C++ reader clamps a phase outside that range and the toolboxes wrap it, but no writer writes one and no reader crashes. |
| [DIS-0037](../discrepancies/DIS-0037-v13-block-durations-from-system.md) | A 1.3 file read with a system of dead times or other rasters | playback | — | No master writer writes a 1.3 file. The readers differ on its block durations only with a non-default system, and no reader crashes on it. |
| [DIS-0055](../discrepancies/DIS-0055-ids-not-positive-or-unique.md) | IDs of events or blocks that are not positive or not unique | playback | — | Both writers number events and blocks from 1. MATLAB's index error on RF ID -2 is on a spec-invalid file, and no reader crashes on the valid file of a repeated block ID. |
| [DIS-0072](../discrepancies/DIS-0072-pypulseq-read-rounds-and-merges-events.md) | Event values with more digits than pypulseq keeps, or equal events with different IDs | playback | — | Both writers write no more digits than pypulseq read keeps, so no written file plays differently. No reader crashes. |
| [DIS-0043](../discrepancies/DIS-0043-unknown-section.md) | A section that the format does not have | acceptance | — | No writer writes an unknown section. On such a file the C++ reader ignores it, and both toolboxes reject it with 'Unknown section code', a deliberate message. |
| [DIS-0044](../discrepancies/DIS-0044-delays-section-after-1-4.md) | A [DELAYS] section in a file of 1.4.0 or later | acceptance | — | No writer writes [DELAYS] in a 1.4+ file. Both toolboxes reject such a file with a deliberate 'MUST NOT contain [DELAYS]' message, and the C++ reader ignores the section. |
| [DIS-0045](../discrepancies/DIS-0045-line-before-first-section.md) | A data line before the first section | acceptance | — | Both writers start the file with comments and [VERSION]. On a data line before the first section, both toolboxes reject with 'Unknown section code', and the C++ reader ignores it. |
| [DIS-0048](../discrepancies/DIS-0048-row-field-count.md) | A row with too few or too many values (a [BLOCKS] row of 7 values, a [TRAP] row of 7) | acceptance | — | No writer writes a row of the wrong length. The C++ reader accepts it silently, and the toolboxes fail on it, but the file is not spec-valid. |
| [DIS-0052](../discrepancies/DIS-0052-adc-dwell-decimal.md) | An ADC dwell time with a decimal point, such as 25000.0 | acceptance | — | Both writers write the dwell as an integer of ns. The C++ reader rejects 25000.0 with a deliberate decode error, which is a rejection, not a crash. |
| [DIS-0058](../discrepancies/DIS-0058-event-longer-than-block.md) | An event that lasts longer than its block | acceptance | — | Neither writer writes a block shorter than its events. The readers accept such a file without the error that the spec requires, but no master writer makes it. |
| [DIS-0067](../discrepancies/DIS-0067-rotation-quaternion-not-normalized.md) | A rotation quaternion that is not normalized, or of norm 0 | acceptance | — | No writer writes a quaternion far from norm 1: MATLAB registerRotationEvent rejects it. No reader crashes; the C++ reader rejects such a file with a message. |
| [DIS-0070](../discrepancies/DIS-0070-signature-of-crlf-file.md) | The [SIGNATURE] hash of a file with CRLF line ends | acceptance | — | On master both writers write LF only (pypulseq since pulseq/pypulseq#429; 1.5.0.post1 writes CRLF on Windows), so neither writes the condition. No reader crashes. |
| [DIS-0071](../discrepancies/DIS-0071-signature-without-type-or-hash.md) | A [SIGNATURE] section without Type or Hash | acceptance | — | Both writers write Type and Hash, so no writer writes the condition. All readers read the file with no crash. |
| [DIS-0035](../discrepancies/DIS-0035-gradient-vertex-off-raster.md) | A vertex of a gradient time shape off the gradient raster (slide 6 against slide 4) | documentation | MATLAB, pypulseq | Both writers write a 3-sample arbitrary gradient with the time shape 0.5 1.5 2.5. Every reader reads the vertices at their times. Only the slides disagree with each other. |
| [DIS-0038](../discrepancies/DIS-0038-event-row-field-counts.md) | The number of fields of an [RF], [GRADIENTS] or [ADC] row (prose against tables and examples) | documentation | MATLAB, pypulseq | Only the spec's prose is wrong. Both writers write rows of 12, 7 and 9 fields as the tables give, and every reader reads them the same way. |
| [DIS-0039](../discrepancies/DIS-0039-extension-string-id-type.md) | An extension header whose STRING_ID is a word (table against examples) | documentation | MATLAB, pypulseq | Only the spec's table is wrong. Both writers write a word as STRING_ID, as the examples give, and every reader reads it. |

| Record | Condition | Priority in the release | Still in | Fixed by | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DIS-0014](../discrepancies/DIS-0014-shapes-last-no-blank-line.md) | [SHAPES] as the last section, with no blank line after its last sample | Medium | pypulseq 1.5.0.post1 | https://github.com/pulseq/pypulseq/pull/359 (commit 36d9fa3) | In pypulseq 1.5.0.post1, read hangs when [SHAPES] ends the file with no blank line.
